cases.answer: It happens when the element you found earlier is no longer attached to the DOM, for example the page re-rendered or you navigated. The fix is to find it again with its locator after the change, usually after an explicit wait for the new state, instead of keeping the old WebElement around. In page objects I keep locators, not cached elements.
